flags.title: NO Medicaid Expansion — Coverage Gap Exists
flags.summary: Georgia has NOT expanded Medicaid. 250K-400K adults between 0-138% FPL have NO coverage pathway. Route to FQHCs, charity care, and ACA marketplace.

flags.title: TANF Benefits Among Lowest in Nation ($280/month)
flags.summary: Georgia TANF provides $280/month for a family of 3 — among the lowest in the country.

flags.title: UI Duration 14-20 Weeks — One of Shortest
flags.summary: Georgia UI duration is 14-20 weeks depending on unemployment rate, one of the shortest in the country.

flags.title: Federal Minimum Wage Only ($7.25/hr)
flags.summary: Georgia has no state minimum wage above the federal $7.25/hr. FLSA is the primary enforcement mechanism.

flags.title: Weakest Tenant Protections in Registry
flags.summary: Georgia has extremely limited tenant protections. Anti-retaliation protections are weak (O.C.G.A. §44-7-23). No rent control. Rapid eviction process.

flags.title: Atlanta Major Refugee Resettlement Hub
flags.summary: Atlanta metro is a significant refugee resettlement hub with Haitian, Congolese, Burmese, and Central American communities.

flags.title: Non-Expansion State Routing Required
flags.summary: Benefits workflows must account for coverage gap. FQHC and charity care pathways are first-line for many uninsured adults.

flags.title: Limited State Civil Rights Enforcement
flags.summary: Georgia Commission on Human Relations has limited enforcement power. Federal agencies (EEOC, HUD) are primary discrimination complaint channels.

flags.title: Involuntary Hold: Georgia Emergency Evaluation
flags.message: GA involuntary psychiatric hold law: Georgia Emergency Evaluation. Statutory authority: O.C.G.A. § 37-3-41. Maximum initial hold duration: 48 hours. Legal standard: danger to self/others. A hearing must be held before the hold can be extended. The person has the right to counsel at the hearing.
action_items: Verify hold did not exceed 48 hours without court order
Confirm hearing was held within statutory timeframe
Check that patient rights notice was provided at admission
Request complete hold documentation from facility

flags.title: Psychiatric Patient Rights
flags.message: Psychiatric patients in GA retain fundamental rights during hospitalization: right to communicate with persons outside the facility, right to receive and send mail, right to access legal counsel, right to refuse treatment (with limited exceptions), right to informed consent, right to access medical records, and right to file grievances. These rights cannot be restricted as a condition of treatment.
action_items: Verify patient rights notice was provided and signed
Check whether any rights were restricted and if proper procedures were followed
Confirm access to legal counsel was not impeded

flags.title: Federal Restraint & Seclusion Limits
flags.message: Federal law (42 CFR § 482.13) sets strict limits on restraint and seclusion in GA: physician order required within 1 hour, face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, continuous monitoring required, maximum 4 hours per order for adults (2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under 9), and restraint may only be used to protect the patient from harm — never as punishment, convenience, or retaliation.
action_items: Request restraint/seclusion logs for all episodes
Verify physician order was obtained within 1 hour
Check that face-to-face evaluation occurred within 1 hour
Verify restraint was not used as punishment or convenience
Check for injuries during restraint episodes
legal_references: CMS State Operations Manual Appendix A

flags.title: Involuntary Psychiatric Hold Statute
flags.message: This state has specific statutes governing involuntary psychiatric holds. Know the time limits, hearing rights, and appeal procedures before they expire.

flags.title: Mental Health Patient Bill of Rights
flags.message: This state has a Patient Bill of Rights for mental health facilities. Facilities must inform patients of these rights upon admission.
flags.statute: Georgia Mental Health Patient Rights Act

flags.title: Discharge Planning Requirements
flags.message: This state requires facilities to create discharge plans with follow-up appointments, medication management, and community resource referrals.
flags.statute: Georgia Mental Health Discharge Planning Standards
